title: credential-fallback-mosaic-stream-progress-unify-sdks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds multi-SDK credential fallback chain and a lightweight stream progress adapter; bumps Python/TS/Go SDK versions. Backwards compatible: default behaviour unchanged unless opt-in. Recommended for early rollout to Dedicated/private customers before wide release.
description: Motivation: Multiple customers and internal workloads observed intermittent auth races during credential rotation under high-throughput streaming workloads. Existing SDKs used slightly different fallback behaviors which made incident diagnosis hard and caused subtle resume failures during token swap. This PR introduces a unified "credential fallback mosaic" -- a small, deterministic chain that attempts delegated token fetch -> cached lease -> orchestrated refresh -> ephemeral token from local agent. It also adds a minimal StreamProgress adapter (emit progress events and checkpoints) to make streaming ergonomics consistent across Python/TS/Go. Implementation notes: - Core credential chain implemented in redwood-core/sdk-common/cred/mosaic.go (Go canonical implementation) and mirrored with idiomatic facades in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript. - StreamProgress adapter added as a thin cross-language surface: progress events are simple JSON envelopes emitted on stream frames (progress, checkpoint, final). Each SDK exposes a small listener callback / async iterator helper to consume these without changing the primary chunking API. - Backoff/retry alignment: introduced a RetryProfile named "streaming-foreground" tuned for low-latency short-circuits and weaker exponential floors to avoid excessive token churn. - Version bumps: python -> 0.27.3, typescript -> 1.9.0, go -> 1.5.2. Compatibility and opt-in: Default behaviour is backward compatible. The mosaic is enabled by default for new clients but preserves previous token lookup order when a legacy config flag (legacyCredOrder=true) is set. StreamProgress is opt-in via a client option (enable_stream_progress=true) to avoid spamming existing applications. Testing: - Unit tests: 86 new unit tests across the three SDKs exercising token failover and progress envelope parsing. - Integration: added a smoke matrix that runs on CI against a staging auth proxy to validate rotation handoffs and stream resume scenarios. - Load canary: a small canary run against Dedicated in us-west-2 with synthetic streams sustained for 4 hours (no auth races observed). Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature gate; 2) Deploy SDK releases to package registries; 3) Canary opt-in with internal repo owners and a handful of early enterprise customers; 4) Full rollout after 2 weeks observation. See linked Linear ENG-981 and ENG-1050 for rollout checklists and postmortem references.
